title: The Beaver Dam
text: Beavers the size of bears have dammed the river, and the valley behind them has drowned. Their dam is a wall of whole trunks, gnawed to points and woven tight. It is the finest timber in the land, and they are watching you look at it.

options.label: Pull timber from their dam, while they are busy watching the water.

outcomes.text: The timber is fine, gnawed to points and hard as bone.
The beavers come. They are the size of bears, with teeth made for felling far bigger things than trees.

options.label: The shrewdest trades with the beavers for their offcuts, and keeps the axes out of sight.

outcomes.text: They drive a hard bargain, chattering, never taking their eyes off your axes.

options.label: Watch how they build, and learn what you can from them.

outcomes.text: It is clever, terrible work. The House carpenters will want to hear of it, though they will not sleep well after.
